To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the utilization of achiral aliphatic amides as ring-formers for the preparation of macrocycles that contain an upper ring junction bearing an aryl substituent is an effective strategy to prepare Grb2 SH 2 domain-binding antagonistic macrocycles.

the utilization of achiral 1,4-disubstituted alkenyl amides as ring-formers for the preparation of Grb2 antagonists by ring-closing olefin metathesis is an efficient strategy that can be used for the preparation of potent Grb2 antagonistic macrocycles.
a series of macrocycles that exhibit Grb2 SH-2 domain binding affinities was prepared by ring-closing olefin metathesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel Grb2 SH-2 domain-binding antagonistic agents for the treatment of human cancer.
the discovery of small molecules that can inhibit the interaction of Grb2 with its binding partners.
the design and synthesis of novel macrocycles that exhibit high Grb2 SH 2 domain-binding affinity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of achirally-substituted alkenyl amina precursors can be used to prepare potent Grb2 antagonists.
the use of achiraly 4-pentynylamides in RCM-derived macrocycles provides an effective means of simplifying the synthesis of Grb2-binding macrocycles.
achiral 4-(1,3-dihydroisobenzofuran-1-ylmethyl) pentenylamide 5d is the most active macrocyclic Grb2 SH 2 domain binder in this series of compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
achiral alkenes, such as 4-pentene, may be utilized to prepare Grb2 SH domain-binding macrocycles of high affinity.
achiral RCM-derived macrocycles bearing cycloalkyl groups at the upper ring-junctions exhibit potent Grb7 SH2 domain-binding activity.
achiral 4-(2-penten-4-yl)benzamide (4a) was synthesized in 3 steps and 2.5% overall yield.
The main takeaway from our work is that
achiral alkenes can be used to prepare macrocycles that are potent Grb2 inhibitors.
the upper ring junction is a critical structural component that is responsible for the potent Grb2-SH2 domain-binding activity of these macrocycles.
a simple, achiral 4-alkenylamide ring-forming component is sufficient to generate macrocycles with potent Grb2-SH2 domain binding affinity.
